question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

She is my **cousin sister.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**cousin sister**" is incorrect because the term "cousin" itself is gender-neutral and does not require an additional gender-specific word.
 
• Adding "sister" or "brother" after "cousin" is unnecessary and redundant.
 
• The correct and concise way to refer to her would simply be "**cousin**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She is my cousin."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "cousin sibling"** – This phrase is incorrect because "sibling" refers to brothers and sisters, and it is redundant when combined with "cousin."
 
• **Option 2: "own cousin"** – This phrase is unnecessary as the word "cousin" already implies a relationship without needing "own."
 
• **Option 3: "cousin girl"** – This phrase is incorrect and ungrammatical because "cousin" does not need a gender-specific qualifier like "girl."
